newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mixed, Eurograde gasoline tight.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mixed, Eurograde gasoline tight.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Thursday.

Gasoline was still tight. A refiner in Italy covered a requirement for Eurograde gasoline on Wednesday and paid a quotes-related number which he said was $1 or $1.50 a tonne above normal purchase levels. Another two similar requirements were outstanding, also in the prompt period.
"The situation is a little bit stressed in Italy at the moment," one dealer said, adding that tight shipping was adding to the problem of a lack of gasoline.
It was thought one refiner with a commitment into Italy may have to resort to bringing material down from Antwerp.
Naphtha was weaker with crude oil. Avails were seen of Turkish material, but were not actively offered.
Gas oil was lower in line with softer northern European
prices which were off on benchmark futures losses but premiums were little changed.
There were signs 0.2 percent gas oil, which has been under pressure from excess Russian material, could be firming up again with the arbitrage door just about open for very large cargoes.
"It's not like a few weeks ago when it was even worthwhile sending over 25,000 tonners. The arb's only open if you can get good freight rates and have a big cargo," said one trader.
Premiums were for 0.2 percent material was assessed at quotes fob +50 cents/+$1.50.
Fuel oil markets were still struggling with the effects of Tuesday's low $75.50 trader to trader deal. But reality was reported to be gradually seeping back into prices.

Swaps were at $77.50/$78.50 for June with physical supply tight, given that cargo demand for bunker spec remains strong and Russians are still scarce. Arb traffic to Singapore was also draining oil out of the market

"When you ask for oil at the moment it's not there," said one trader, adding that dealers were already discussing July material. One Spanish buyer was heard prepared to pay $2 over cif Med quotes for bunker spec.
Better Russian supplies were seen from the start of next week -- London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
